text:
elaine: Heads-up — customer reported odd behavior when we swapped their hosted model from `redwood-embed-v1` -> `redwood-embed-v2` while also rotating signed URLs. They saw 401s for embeddings calls for a few minutes, but text gen worked fine.

samir: Ugh. Did they rotate the client key at the same time as model swap?

elaine: They rotated the signed upload URL for user content (S3 presigned) and then ran a migration script that updated model= in the request body. Error was specifically `401 Unauthorized: signature mismatch` for the embeddings endpoint.

tay: Quick Q: are embeddings requests routed differently for model variants? We do model routing + auth checking in the front door service — should be the same path.

ben: They might be hitting cached route metadata that still referenced old signer config. If front door kept an old model->backend mapping for a short TTL, and the upload URL rotation changed signature expectations, that could cause mismatch. But 401 on embeddings suggests auth layer, not model mapping.

samir: Can you paste the failing curl (sanitized)?

elaine: Sure — here is a redacted example they sent:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v2","input":"...","user_upload_url":"https://s3.aws/signed?X-Amz-Signature=OLDSIG"}'
```

elaine: The `user_upload_url` had the old signature; after client re-requested a fresh presigned URL, requests succeeded.

tay: So two things interleaved: signed URL rotation + model swap. Docs angle: we should call this out in the migration guide as a race condition where assets referenced by requests might be signed under a different auth epoch.

ben: Agreed. Proposal for docs PR: small section in "Model swap checklist" titled "Signed assets & short-lived credentials" that warns to:
- rotate signatures then re-issue references before bulk migration
- flush/refresh client-side caches of presigned URLs
- run a small smoke test hitting embeddings endpoint per user after rotation

samir: Also add an SDK snippet that demonstrates a safe pattern: request new presigned url, upload, then call embeddings. Show exponential backoff on 401s for the first minute.

elaine: I'll draft a short snippet. Example (JS):

```js
// get upload URL
const { url } = await api.get('/uploads/presign', { userId });
// upload
await fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: file });
// then call embeddings with the returned url
await redwood.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood-embed-v2', input, user_upload_url: url });
```

elaine: Add note: if you rotate keys server-side, ensure any long-lived client state that stores presigned URLs is invalidated first.

tay: One more edge-case: older SDKs used optimistic model hints in the client (v0.9 SDK would send `model_hint` header) — if backend mapping changed we should make sure fallback to canonical model name is documented. Add a line: "Avoid optimistic model hints during migration; prefer explicit model names and confirm post-swap."

ben: Okay. Action items:
- elaine: open PR in docs repo with the signed-assets section + JS and curl snippets (include link to their support thread) — target EOD today
- samir: add backoff example and mention 401 behavior in SDK migration guide
- tay: add note about model-hint header and link to runtime routing doc

docs-bot: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2268 by elaine — draft: "Model swap: signed assets & auth race conditions" :eyes:

elaine: pinging @samir @tay for quick review once PR is up. I'll also add an internal playbook checklist for SREs to run a 1-user smoke test per region after swaps.

samir: thanks — this is a subtle one, good catch by support.

tay: lgtm, small copy edits only.

ben: I'll add a test case to the migration smoke harness to simulate rotated presigned URLs and expect a retry path.

elaine: Great. Closing thread once PR merges. :white_check_mark:
